title: How can one figure have three acute, one right and two obtuse angles?
description: Four rays from one point make six angles, one for each pair of rays. Placing the rays at zero, thirty, sixty and one hundred fifty degrees gives three acute angles, one right angle and two obtuse angles.
teaching_notes: One idea: n rays from one point make an angle for every pair, so four rays make six angles, and the ray directions decide their kinds. Watch for students who expect the figure to be a six-sided shape.

video_script.why: The child sees that rays from one point make an angle for every pair, and places the rays so that the six angles have the required kinds.
video_script.substitution: Rays from a point at 0, 30, 60 and 150 degrees; find each angle by taking the smaller direction from the larger and name it by comparing with 90 and 180.
video_script.anchor: an empty board with a protractor, ready to draw rays from a point O
video_script.payoff_line: Four rays make six angles, three acute, one right and two obtuse

final_answer.value: four rays from O at 0°, 30°, 60° and 150°: three acute, one right and two obtuse angles
final_answer.spoken: four rays from the point O at zero, thirty, sixty and one hundred fifty degrees make three acute, one right and two obtuse angles

never_show: a six-sided shape with three acute, one right and two obtuse angles
maths_rules: acute: less than 90°; obtuse: more than 90° and less than 180°
four rays from a point make 4 x 3 / 2 = 6 angles, one for each pair
rays at 0, 30, 60 and 150 degrees: AOB = 30, BOC = 30, AOC = 60, COD = 90, BOD = 120, AOD = 150
video_script.design: One point O with a base ray. Rays are added one by one with the protractor; arcs are coloured teal for acute, grey for right and amber for obtuse.
open_questions: The worklist and book answer suggest a hexagon ABCDEF; a simple six-sided shape cannot have six angles all under 180 degrees with these kinds, because the six angles of a hexagon add to 720 and these kinds add to less than 720, so this video uses four rays from one point instead.
